Hi Samantha — quick note on telemetry and cookies from the product/SE side. Apologies for the longish email; wanted to be explicit.

Console (console.redwood.ai):
- Telemetry: We collect anonymized usage metrics (API call counts, UI feature usage), error/trace telemetry for debugging, and aggregated performance metrics (latency histograms).
- PII: We do not ingest user-entered PII for analytics. Request/response payloads are not used for product analytics.
- Cookies: We use a session cookie for auth and a separate analytics cookie (first-party) to measure UI interactions.
- Opt-out: Org admins can disable UI analytics entirely from the Admin > Privacy settings (toggle labeled "Disable UI analytics"). This prevents analytics cookie from being set for console users.

Docs site (docs.redwood.ai):
- We use Google Analytics (configurable) and a small set of non-essential cookies for site analytics. The docs site supports a cookie banner with opt-out (documented). We can serve a cookie-free version for enterprise customers on request.

Hosted vs Dedicated/Private differences:
- Hosted API: request logs used for debugging are retained per our retention policy (default 30 days for most customers); we offer configurable retention for enterprise customers.
- Dedicated/Private: customers control telemetry collection in Private deployments; we can disable telemetry and integrate with customer-managed logging if required.

Docs link: https://docs.redwood.ai/security/telemetry — this page includes cookie names, retention windows, and admin controls.

Happy to jump on a 20-min screen share to show where the toggles live.

— Vivek
